title: Rabbi David Tawil: Baruch Hashem

chapters.title: Introduction and the phrase of thanking Hashem
chapters.about: Daily mentions of Hashem,Baal Shemtov,Jewish awareness of God

chapters.title: Biblical figures who said Blessed is Hashem
chapters.about: Yosef,Surprise that patriarchs didn't say it first,Yitro, Noach, and Eliezer

chapters.title: The universal message of Parashat Yitro
chapters.about: Yitro's transformation,Judaism's view of non-Jews,Spreading awareness of God

chapters.title: Dividing the Ten Commandments
chapters.about: Rabbi Jonathan Sacks' categorization,Groups of three,Creation and social institutions

summary: Rabbi Tawil explores the meaning of expressing gratitude to Hashem in daily life, connecting the phrase to unexpected biblical figures like Noah, Eliezer, and Yitro. He discusses Parashat Yitro and the universal message of Judaism, alongside Rabbi Jonathan Sacks' grouping of the Ten Commandments and how gratitude serves as an antidote to jealousy.
questions: Why are non-Jewish figures in the Torah the first to say 'Blessed is Hashem'?
What is the connection between Parashat Yitro and the giving of the Torah?
How can the Ten Commandments be divided into groups of three, plus the tenth?
What is the relationship between jealousy and the Ten Commandments?
How does gratitude act as an antidote to envy?
